events.note: Hand-written dated events, researched and not yet attended. Sport fixtures here fill the Watch half of Sport; each is checked against the team's or organiser's own schedule on the date given.

items.title: Valkyries in the playoffs
items.why: The Valkyries won their first playoff game on Sunday, 104 to 80 over Dallas in front of a roaring Chase Center, in only their second season. The first round is best of three: Game 2 is in Dallas on Wednesday, and if it goes to a Game 3 it is back at Chase Center on Friday 2 October. Tickets go the moment it is confirmed.
items.source: Golden State Valkyries; NBC Bay Area; SF Standard
items.hoursNote: A Game 3, if needed, on Friday 2 October at Chase Center — time set by the WNBA

items.title: Sharks home opener v Panthers
items.priceNote: Tickets from ~$40; the street festival is free
items.why: The first home game of the Sharks' season, against the Florida Panthers, both Tkachuk brothers included. Puck drop is at seven. Before it, the streets outside SAP Center become a free festival with food stalls, player interviews and giveaways, so come early even without a ticket. Caltrain to Diridon is across the road.
items.source: San Jose Sharks; The Hockey News

items.title: 49ers v Broncos
items.why: A Sunday home game at Levi's, kick-off 1:25. Do not drive: take Caltrain to Mountain View and the VTA light rail to Great America, which is on the stadium's doorstep. The lots open hours ahead for tailgating, and the sun is fierce in the east stands, so sit on the west side if you can.

items.title: Fleet Week and the Blue Angels
items.times: Air show noon to 4pm, Friday to Sunday; ships from October 4
items.why: The Blue Angels are back after the 2025 shutdown grounded them. The air show fills the sky between the Golden Gate and Alcatraz from noon to four each day, the Friday morning starts with the Parade of Ships, and navy ships are open for tours at Piers 35 and 27 on October 7 and 8. Watching from the shore costs nothing.
items.spectator: Marina Green, Crissy Field or Fort Mason, which has Equator Coffees at the gate. Arrive by eleven with a blanket and layers.
items.source: Fleet Week San Francisco; SF Chronicle; ABC7

items.title: Stanford v Elon — Homecoming
items.why: Homecoming weekend at Stanford: the campus at its liveliest, the stadium full of alumni, and the band on the field. Kick-off is 4:30. Tickets are cheap, and you can walk from downtown Palo Alto up Palm Drive.

items.title: Earthquakes v Nashville
items.why: A Saturday-night MLS game at PayPal Park, with the season's playoff places being decided. Get there early for the huge open-air bar behind one goal, and stand with the supporters if you want to sing.

items.title: Bay FC v Portland Thorns
items.why: The Bay's women's team against Portland, the NWSL's best-supported club, on a Sunday afternoon at two. Bay FC is only in its third season and the crowd is young, loud and growing. It is the next-to-last home game of the regular season.

items.title: 49ers v Commanders — Monday night
items.why: Monday Night Football at Levi's, with Keena Turner inducted into the 49ers Hall of Fame at half-time. Kick-off is 5:15, so leave work early and take VTA light rail from Mountain View rather than joining the traffic on 101.

items.title: Warriors home opener v Grizzlies
items.priceNote: Expensive — the opener is the hardest ticket of the year
items.why: The first home game of the Warriors' season, against Memphis, at seven. It is the hardest ticket of the year at Chase Center, with the banners and the introductions before tip-off. Take Muni's T line to the Chase Center stop, or walk from the Caltrain at 4th and King in fifteen minutes.

items.title: Stanford v NC State
items.why: Friday the 23rd or Saturday the 24th — the ACC has not fixed the day yet, so check before you plan around it.

items.title: Earthquakes v Colorado
items.why: A Wednesday-night game at PayPal Park, and the cheapest way into a Quakes match all season. Caltrain to Santa Clara and a short walk.

items.title: Stanford v Cal volleyball
items.priceNote: Cheap — if you can get one
items.why: The rivalry match in one of the best women's volleyball programmes in the country, on a Friday night at Maples. It is the home match that sells out first, so buy as soon as single tickets go on sale. Stanford also plays Virginia Tech and Virginia at home on 2 and 3 October if this one is gone.

items.title: Warriors v Lakers
items.why: The Lakers at Chase Center a week into the season, and a game that counts in the NBA Cup group stage. It is the biggest regular-season ticket of the autumn.
items.hoursNote: Friday night — tip-off time set with the NBA Cup schedule

items.title: Earthquakes v Real Salt Lake — the home finale
items.why: The last home game of the regular season, on Halloween, so expect costumes in the stands. If the Quakes are in the playoff hunt this is the one to go to.
items.hoursNote: Saturday, Halloween — kick-off time to be confirmed

items.title: Bay FC v San Diego Wave
items.why: Bay FC's last home game of the regular season, a California derby against San Diego on a Sunday afternoon.

items.title: 49ers v Raiders
items.why: The old Bay Area rivalry, now that the Raiders play in Las Vegas, and the loudest regular-season game at Levi's. It is a Sunday at 1:05. Take the train: Caltrain to Mountain View, then VTA light rail to Great America.

items.title: The Big Game: Cal v Stanford
items.why: The 129th Big Game, one of the oldest rivalries in college football, played since 1892 for a trophy that is literally a hatchet: the Stanford Axe. It is Cal's turn to host, in the stadium in Strawberry Canyon. Take BART to Downtown Berkeley and walk up with the crowd. Wear red or blue, not both.
items.source: Cal Athletics; Stanford Athletics; SF Chronicle
items.hoursNote: Saturday — kick-off time is set by TV a couple of weeks before

items.title: Stanford v SMU
items.why: The last home game of Stanford's season, on Thanksgiving Saturday, when the campus is empty and the stadium is not. Cheap tickets, a walk up Palm Drive, and a good way to get out of the house after Thursday.
items.hoursNote: Kick-off not announced yet — the schedule has it once it is

items.title: 49ers v Seahawks
items.why: The division rival, at home on the Sunday after Thanksgiving at 1:25. It often decides the division. Caltrain and VTA light rail to Great America, as for every game here.

items.title: PWHL San Jose's first home game
items.priceNote: Tickets on sale through the PWHL
items.why: The first home game of the Bay Area's first professional women's hockey team: the new San Jose side against the Minnesota Frost, the league's first two champions, at four on a Saturday. The PWHL has sold out arenas in its other cities. Be there for the first one.

places.note: The curated tier. Hand-written, and empty is honest.

items.title: Mademoiselle Colette
items.why: Come for the almond croissant, flaky right through and very good. It's a day-old croissant split, filled with almond cream and baked a second time, which is why the outside shatters. It's a French bakery-café on Lytton, a short walk from the University Avenue cafés.
items.imageSubject: An almond croissant outside Mademoiselle Colette

items.title: Bacio di Latte
items.why: A favourite for coffee and gelato under one roof. It's a Brazilian gelateria, the chain's first in the Bay Area, open since this spring, with gelato made in-house every day from Clover organic milk. There are more than twenty flavours, and the affogato bar brings the two halves together: espresso poured over a scoop.
items.coordsFrom: the shopping centre (osm way/110163462); the shop is not mapped yet
items.imageSubject: A coffee outside Bacio di Latte

items.title: HP Garage
items.why: The birthplace of Silicon Valley: Bill Hewlett and Dave Packard started the company in this garage in 1938, and it is a California Historical Landmark. HP restored the house, garage and shed to how they looked in 1939. It is not open for tours. HP says you may look and take photographs from the sidewalk. It is a quiet residential street, so keep it short and keep it quiet.
items.source: Wikipedia; hpmuseum.org; HP; existence and position confirmed against OpenStreetMap (node/1710414037)
items.hoursFrom: seen from the pavement — it is a private house

items.title: Friday Night Waltz
items.area: First United Methodist Church, 625 Hamilton Avenue
items.why: A dance evening every Friday near the Caltrain station. It starts with a lesson, then an intermediate one, then a DJ until late. Mostly waltz, with polka, tango, swing and salsa in between. You don't need a partner: the classes rotate partners quickly, so it is a good first try even if you have never done any of it.
items.source: fridaynightwaltz.com; Yelp; the church confirmed against OpenStreetMap (way/131995317)
items.cadence: Fridays · a lesson, then dancing until late
items.firstStep: $15 at the door — no partner needed

items.title: Palo Alto Art Center
items.why: The city's own art centre, by Rinconada Park. Adult classes run in terms: painting, drawing, mixed media, jewellery, and ceramics, with a proper ceramics studio and kilns. It is the place to learn to throw a pot without paying private-studio prices. The galleries are worth a look while you're there.
items.source: City of Palo Alto; Palo Alto Online; confirmed against OpenStreetMap (way/231246592)
items.firstStep: Register for the season through the City of Palo Alto

items.title: Sunset sail — Adventure Cat
items.area: Pier 39, Gate J, by the sea lions
items.why: Sailing under the Golden Gate as the sun goes down behind it is unforgettable. It's ninety minutes on a catamaran out of Pier 39, and the city lights come on behind you on the way back. Bring a jacket: it's cold on the water even after a warm day. Locals get 20% off on Mondays with the code SFLOCAL.
items.coordsFrom: Pier 39 (osm way/128240121); the boat is not mapped
items.hoursNote: Sails around sunset, so the departure moves with the season — the booking calendar has the day’s time

items.title: Molly Tea
items.why: Tea and matcha drinks built on jasmine and other floral teas, from a Chinese fragrant-tea chain. This is its fourth Bay Area shop, open since last November. Expect a line; service is quick, so it moves faster than it looks.
items.coordsFrom: the building at 310–318 University Avenue (osm way/133116320); the shop itself is not mapped yet
items.hoursFrom: the Chowbus and Apple Maps listings

items.title: The Filbert Steps
items.why: Wooden stairs down the steep east side of Telegraph Hill, where the street gives out, through cottage gardens residents have tended for decades. You can't see them from anywhere else in the city. Go down them rather than up.

items.title: Sutro Baths ruins
items.why: The concrete ruins of an enormous Victorian bathhouse, opened in 1896, which burned in 1966. It sits in a cove at the edge of the Pacific below Lands End. You can walk the old walls and the tunnel through the rock. It is best at sunset, and it is part of the national recreation area, so it's free.
items.source: National Park Service; Wikipedia; confirmed against OpenStreetMap (way/32776564)
items.hoursFrom: nps.gov — Lands End is open from 6am until an hour after sunset
items.hoursNote: 6am to an hour after sunset

items.title: The Wave Organ
items.area: The end of the Marina jetty
items.why: An acoustic sculpture at the end of the Marina jetty: pipes set into granite and marble from a demolished cemetery, played by the waves. It is loudest at high tide and nearly silent at low, so check the tide first. It opened in 1986, and the view back across the harbour to the city is its own reason to go.
items.hoursNote: An outdoor sculpture at the end of the jetty, free and unfenced — it sounds best at high tide

items.title: Balmy Alley murals
items.why: One block of the Mission, between 24th and 25th, painted end to end: garage doors and fences covered in murals since the early 1970s, many about Central America and the neighbourhood itself. They are repainted as they fade, so it is never the same twice. Walk it on the way to 24th Street's bakeries and taquerías.
items.source: Wikipedia; Precita Eyes; confirmed against OpenStreetMap (way/8920344)

items.title: Equator Coffees — Fort Mason
items.area: 2 Marina Boulevard, at the Fort Mason gate
items.why: The view is the reason: the café sits in the old Army gatehouse at the entrance to Fort Mason, right on the Bay Trail, looking straight across the water to the Golden Gate. It's lively all day, with cyclists and runners stopping on their way along the waterfront. Come for an espresso in the morning, or late in the day for the sunset over the bridge.
items.coordsFrom: Fort Mason Center (osm node/358857198); the café is at its entrance and is not mapped itself
items.imageCredit: Original uploader was SuperJumbo at en.wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0

items.title: Oren's Hummus
items.why: The original Oren's, open on University since 2011. Oren Dobronsky, a start-up founder from Tel Aviv, opened it because he couldn't find hummus in Silicon Valley like the hummus at home. Order a bowl of the warm hummus with fresh pita and whatever is on top. It is quick, casual and always busy.

items.title: Ettan
items.why: California-Indian cooking from Srijith Gopinathan, who earned two Michelin stars at Campton Place in San Francisco, in a downtown room that opened in 2020. It is listed in the Michelin Guide, and its team were James Beard finalists in 2026. Book ahead: it is the one for a special dinner.

items.title: Rooh
items.why: Progressive Indian on University since 2020: a live-fire grill, classic dishes reworked with modern technique, desserts made in house, and a cocktail list to match. It is the sister of the Rooh on Brannan Street in San Francisco.

items.title: Khazana
items.why: The first American restaurant from the celebrity chef Sanjeev Kapoor, which opened on University in 2024. The menu travels across every region of India and borrows from outside it.

items.title: Pho Ha Noi
items.why: The pho on University Avenue, a Cupertino favourite that opened a Palo Alto branch in 2023. The room is spacious and the bowls are generous. Order the pho dac biet, the combination beef, and add the imperial crab rolls.
items.source: Yelp; Essential Palo Alto Restaurants; confirmed against OpenStreetMap (way/132527976)

items.title: Local Union 271
items.why: A farm-to-table American restaurant and bar on University, sourcing from a circle of local farms, ranches and breweries. It has a patio, weekend brunch, and a happy hour from 4 to 7 when plates and drinks are $6 each. That's the best time to come.

items.title: Bevri
items.why: The Bay Area's only Georgian restaurant. Order two things. The khachapuri is a boat of bread filled with molten cheese and an egg: stir it together and tear off the crust to dip. The khinkali are big twisted dumplings full of broth: hold them by the knot, bite, and drink the soup before the rest.
items.source: bevri.com; Palo Alto Online; confirmed against OpenStreetMap (way/132883462)
items.imageSubject: Georgian chokha coats at the door of Bevri

items.title: Taverna
items.why: Hellenic farm-to-table cooking on Emerson, opened in 2018 by two Palo Alto locals who met working at Evvia. Start with the crispy anchovies, grilled octopus and halloumi, then the souvlaki. There is weekend brunch too.
items.source: Palo Alto Online; tavernarestaurant.net; confirmed against OpenStreetMap (way/132296678)

items.title: Maruwu Seicha
items.why: Matcha every way you could want it: as soft serve, as gelato, in a tart, or as a latte, with roasted hojicha too. The line is worth waiting in. It's just as good a place to settle in with a laptop and work through the afternoon, cup in hand. It's the Palo Alto café of a Kyoto tea company, on University since October 2024.
items.imageSubject: A matcha latte outside Maruwu Seicha, University Avenue

items.title: Meyhouse
items.priceNote: Meze $13–19, mains $18–42; chef's tasting menu $95 a head
items.why: A Turkish meyhane on Emerson: a long evening of meze, grilled fish and raki, in the high-ceilinged room that used to be Gordon Biersch. About half the menu is the chef-owner's family recipes, the yogurt is made in-house, and he threw the plates himself. Order the Turkish bread, the grilled octopus on fava purée, the eggplant dishes and the manti dumplings, then künefe to finish. It gets loud when it is full, so book. On most Friday and Saturday nights it is also a jazz supper club, with seatings at five and eight.
items.source: meyhouserestaurant.com; Food Gal (2023); OpenTable; confirmed against OpenStreetMap (way/132397113)

items.title: Pizzeria Delfina
items.why: The Palo Alto branch of the Mission pizzeria: Neapolitan-style pies from a wood oven, fresh pasta and a seasonal list of antipasti. Reviewers single out the meatballs and the Napoletana, and the panna cotta for dessert. A gluten-free crust is available.
items.imageSubject: Pizzeria Delfina on Emerson Street at night

items.title: Evvia Estiatorio
items.why: Palo Alto's Greek institution since 1995, and the sister of Kokkari in San Francisco. It is a warm room of wooden beams, copper pots and a wood-burning fireplace, and most of the menu comes off the wood grill. The lamb chops are why people come back. Add the octopus and the grilled vegetable skewers with garlicky yogurt. It is in the Michelin Guide, and dinner books up.
items.source: evvia.net; Michelin Guide; OpenTable; confirmed against OpenStreetMap (way/132527968)

items.title: Nobu Palo Alto
items.priceNote: Expensive; Tanoshi hour 3–5 in the lounge is the cheaper way in
items.why: Nobu Matsuhisa's Japanese–Peruvian menu on the ground floor of the Nobu Hotel: black cod with miso, yellowtail with jalapeño, and the rest of the dishes that made the name. The lobby lounge has a Tanoshi hour from 3 to 5 every day, and the garden serves afternoon tea at weekends.
items.coordsFrom: the Nobu Hotel, still mapped under its old name Epiphany Hotel (osm way/132397111); the restaurant is on its ground floor
items.imageSubject: Nobu on Hamilton Avenue at night

items.title: Marufuku Ramen
items.why: The San Francisco Japantown ramen shop's Palo Alto branch, opened in early 2026 in the old Starbucks on University. It serves Hakata-style tonkotsu, a milky pork broth that simmers for hours, with thin, firm noodles, and there is beer, sake and cocktails. It seats about fifty, so expect a wait at peak times.
items.coordsFrom: the address point for 374 University Avenue (osm way/675214190); the restaurant is not mapped yet
items.imageSubject: Marufuku Ramen on University Avenue at night

items.title: Palo Alto Junior Museum & Zoo
items.why: The city's science museum and small zoo, built for young children: hands-on exhibits, and animals you can watch up close. Book a timed entry online first, because they can't guarantee walk-ins. Parking is free in the lot and on the street nearby.
items.priceNote: $16 weekday mornings and weekends, $12 weekday afternoons; $3 income-eligible; under 12 months free
items.hoursFrom: paloaltozoo.org — open Tuesday to Sunday, 10am to 5pm

items.title: Bedwell Bayfront Park
items.why: A flat 160-acre park on the Bay's edge, with a 2.3-mile loop of the Bay Trail through meadows and salt marsh. It's the easy sunset walk on this side of the Peninsula, and the gates stay open until sunset (as late as 9pm in midsummer). Dogs are welcome on a leash. It's one of the few nearby places where they are.
items.dogsNote: Pets on leash and under full control at all times (City of Menlo Park)
items.source: City of Menlo Park; position from OpenStreetMap way/28570810
items.hoursFrom: menlopark.gov — gates open at 7am, closing from 5:30pm in December to 9pm in June and July
items.hoursNote: Gates open at 7am and close at sunset, between 5:30pm in December and 9pm in midsummer

items.title: Mitchell Park and the Magical Bridge playground
items.why: Palo Alto's biggest park has the Magical Bridge, an inclusive playground built so children of every ability can play together. Beside it are picnic areas, lawns and a renovated fenced dog park with separate sides for small dogs and mixed sizes. So a family with a dog can do the whole outing here.
items.dogsNote: Dogs on a leash in the park (City of Palo Alto, code 6.16.100); the fenced dog park is the off-leash part
items.source: City of Palo Alto; position from OpenStreetMap way/26662981
items.hoursNote: Open daily; the playground's own hours are on the city's park page

items.title: Saint Michael's Alley
items.why: Palo Alto's oldest story in a dining room. It opened in 1959 on University Avenue as the first coffeehouse on the Peninsula, where Joan Baez sang early on and the Grateful Dead played, and moved to the corner of Homer and Emerson in 1974. Today it is a relaxed neighbourhood restaurant with seasonal Californian cooking and a dinner menu that changes every three months. Weekend brunch is the local favourite, and the Annex next door on Emerson does it too.
items.source: stmikes.com; Palo Alto History (paloaltohistory.org); confirmed against OpenStreetMap
items.coordsFrom: the map pin for Saint Michael's Alley

items.title: Mendocino Farms
items.why: A bright, easy sandwich-and-salad counter a block off University, good for a quick lunch that still feels generous. The menu turns over with the seasons, alongside regulars like the chicken pesto sandwich and the chinese chicken salad, and there are plenty of vegetarian options. Two hours of free parking in the High and Hamilton lot behind it.

items.title: Sweet Maple
items.why: The Palo Alto branch of the Fillmore brunch spot, open since January 2022 and still with a queue on weekends. Everyone comes for the Millionaire's Bacon, thick slabs baked with brown sugar and cayenne, which the restaurant has trademarked; the deep-fried French toast is the other famous plate. Go early or on a weekday to skip the wait.
items.source: Palo Alto Online (February 2022); sweetmaplesf.com; confirmed against OpenStreetMap
items.coordsFrom: the map pin for Sweet Maple

items.title: Rangoon Ruby
items.why: Burmese cooking downtown, in a warm room with a good cocktail list. Start with the tea leaf salad, fermented tea leaves with crunchy beans, nuts, tomato and cabbage, mixed at the table; after that, the platha with curry dip, the rainbow salad and the garlic noodles are the usual order. The mains are made for sharing, so bring a few people.
items.source: rangoonrubypa.com; Palo Alto Online review (2014); confirmed against OpenStreetMap
items.coordsFrom: the map pin for Rangoon Ruby

items.title: Zaytinya
items.why: José Andrés's mezze restaurant, which began in Washington in 2002 and opened its first Bay Area room at the shopping centre on 1 December 2025, in part of the old Macy's. The menu moves between Turkish, Greek and Lebanese small plates: puffy pita straight from the oven, hummus, crispy brussels afelia and lamb kebabs. Order a lot, share everything, and book ahead for dinner.
items.source: zaytinya.com; Palo Alto Online (November 2025); Food Gal (December 2025)
items.coordsFrom: the shopping centre (osm way/110163462); the restaurant is not mapped yet

items.title: Delarosa
items.why: Roman-style pizza with a thin, crackly crust from the team behind Wildseed and Super Duper, open since November 2025 where California Pizza Kitchen used to be. Beyond the pizzas there are antipasti, skewers and pasta; try the Capricciosa or the Bartender, with burrata and spicy fennel sausage. Easy with children: there's a kids' menu and crayons on the table.
items.source: delarosasf.com; Palo Alto Online (July 2025); Metro Silicon Valley
items.coordsFrom: the old California Pizza Kitchen pin (the same unit)

items.title: Dumpling Time
items.why: The San Francisco dumpling house's first Peninsula branch, open since May 2025. Dumplings are folded by hand where you can watch: soup dumplings, har gow and the pan-fried potstickers are the ones to get, with noodles and bao for the rest of the table. A quick, reliable lunch between shops.
items.source: Palo Alto Online (April 2025); the Stanford Shopping Center directory
items.coordsFrom: the shopping centre (osm way/110163462); the restaurant is not mapped yet

items.title: RH Rooftop Restaurant
items.why: Lunch in a glass box on the third floor of the RH furniture gallery: a skylit courtyard with heritage olive trees, chandeliers and a limestone fountain, with views out to the hills. The food is classic and polished, and the truffle fries, the lobster roll and the crispy artichokes are what people order. It's more about the room than the kitchen, which makes it a good place for a long weekend brunch.
items.source: rh.com; The Infatuation; SFGate; confirmed against OpenStreetMap
items.coordsFrom: the map pin for RH Rooftop Restaurant

items.title: La Baguette
items.why: A busy French bakery-café in the middle of the shopping centre, with tables outside. Breads and pastries are baked on site every day without preservatives: croissants, pains au chocolat and fruit tarts to go with a coffee, or a sandwich on a fresh baguette for lunch between shops.
items.source: the Stanford Shopping Center directory; confirmed against OpenStreetMap
items.coordsFrom: the map pin for La Baguette

items.title: Kirk's Steakburgers
items.why: Burgers ground by hand every day and grilled over an open charcoal fire, as they have been since the family opened the first Kirk's on El Camino in 1948. Nothing fancy: a thick steakburger, fries and a shake, and a toppings bar to finish it yourself. A Midtown institution for students and families alike.
items.coordsFrom: the map pin for Kirk's Steakburgers

items.title: Philz Coffee
items.why: The San Francisco chain that makes every cup to order, one pour-over at a time, in a blend you pick from the board. The Forest Avenue shop opens before five in the morning and fills with laptops by nine. Try the Mint Mojito iced coffee, the one everybody orders.
items.coordsFrom: the map pin for Philz Coffee

items.title: Covour Coffee
items.why: A small roastery café in Midtown known for pretty, inventive lattes flavoured with ube, pandan and tiramisu, and for its pandan mochi. Calm enough to study in during the week.
items.source: covourcoffee.com; Yelp; placed by its address point (OpenStreetMap node/2399562224)
items.coordsFrom: the address point for 2706 Middlefield Road (osm node/2399562224); the café is not mapped yet

items.title: Yummy Future
items.why: A robot barista makes the drinks at this café, open since October 2025 in the old American Apparel. Order a matcha latte with strawberry cream or a black sesame drink. With about forty seats, charging ports, whiteboards on the walls and hours until nine or ten at night, it has become a late study spot.
items.source: Palo Alto Online (November 2025); confirmed against OpenStreetMap
items.coordsFrom: the map pin for Yummy Future

items.title: CoHo
items.why: The Coffee House in Stanford's student union: coffee, beer and wine, sandwiches and a big patio, and the closest thing campus has to a living room. It is busiest on nights with live music or a game on the screens, and it stays open until eleven midweek.

items.title: Cantor Arts Center
items.why: Stanford's art museum, free to everyone, with collections from antiquity to now. Outside is the Rodin Sculpture Garden, one of the largest collections of Rodin bronzes outside Paris, including The Gates of Hell; it's open at all hours and lit at night, which makes it a favourite evening walk. The Anderson Collection of modern American art is next door.
items.coordsFrom: the map pin for Cantor Arts Center

items.title: Café Borrone
items.why: A big European-style café next to Kepler's Books, with a fountain on the patio. It's Menlo Park's meeting place: coffee meetings, founders pitching over breakfast, a slow lunch in the sun. Free parking underground.

items.title: Scratch
items.why: A comfortable Castro Street restaurant with a patio, doing American comfort food from scratch, as the name says. The weekday happy hour from four to six fills with the tech crowd; weekend brunch is the other draw.
items.coordsFrom: the address point for 401 Castro Street (osm way/635376259)
items.imageSubject: Castro Street at Villa, Mountain View

items.title: Google Visitor Experience
items.why: The one part of Google's campus the public can walk into, at the new Bay View buildings under their curved, scaly solar roof. There is a café open to everyone, a Google shop, a small exhibit and changing art, plus events. Walk on to Shoreline Lake afterwards.
items.source: visit.withgoogle.com; Metro Silicon Valley; confirmed against OpenStreetMap (node/11721651966)

items.title: Apple Park Visitor Center
items.why: The public face of Apple's ring-shaped headquarters, in a glass and stone building by Foster + Partners. There's an Apple Store, an augmented-reality model of the campus, a café, and a roof terrace that looks across to the ring building itself. The campus is closed to visitors, so this is as close as you get.
items.source: apple.com; Foster + Partners; confirmed against OpenStreetMap (way/518295584)

items.title: Main Street Cupertino
items.why: A short outdoor high street of restaurants and shops across from Apple Park's south side, where a lot of Apple lunches and team dinners happen. Lazy Dog, Eureka!, Kula revolving sushi and a row of Asian cafés and dessert shops; a green in the middle has summer events.
items.hoursFrom: public streets; each shop and restaurant keeps its own hours

items.title: Marufuku Ramen
items.why: The Cupertino branch of the Japantown ramen shop: Hakata-style tonkotsu, a rich, milky pork broth with thin, firm noodles. A lunchtime favourite near Apple Park, so expect a wait at noon.

items.title: Gochi Japanese Fusion Tapas
items.why: A Japanese izakaya where you sit shoeless at low tables and share small plates: seared salmon, fried chicken, uni pasta and the famous pizzas on a thin rice crust. One of Cupertino's best-loved dinners, so book.

items.title: Mian Sichuan Noodles & Dumplings
items.why: Chongqing street noodles, fiery and numbing with Sichuan pepper, plus wontons in chilli oil and dan dan noodles. Fast, cheap and good for a weekday lunch near the Apple offices.
items.coordsFrom: the address point for 19389 Stevens Creek Boulevard (osm way/387051751)

items.title: Buck's of Woodside
items.why: The diner where Silicon Valley does its deals: since the 1990s founders have pitched venture capitalists over breakfast here, and Netscape, PayPal, Hotmail and Tesla are among the companies with early meetings at these tables. The room is crammed with oddities hanging from the ceiling. Go for breakfast, and look around.
items.source: buckswoodside.com; Wikipedia; NPR (2010); confirmed against OpenStreetMap (node/423370577)

items.title: Santana Row
items.why: A European-style outdoor street of about thirty restaurants and fifty shops, the place people across the South Bay go for a night out. Walk it in the evening when the patios fill; Augustine, Suspiro and Meso are among the restaurants to try, and there's a cinema, live music in the park and a Wednesday farmers' market in summer.
items.source: santanarow.com; Visit San José; confirmed against OpenStreetMap (way/142697822)
items.hoursFrom: public streets; each shop and restaurant keeps its own hours

items.title: Orchard Valley Coffee
items.why: Downtown Campbell's own roastery and living room, on a corner of the main street, with big open windows and an old brick fireplace. They roast the beans and bake the pastries in-house, and there's live music some evenings.
items.source: orchardvalleycoffee.net; Downtown Campbell; Metro Silicon Valley (2019)

items.title: Lookout Coffee
items.why: A bright specialty-coffee bar on Winchester, a few minutes' walk from downtown Campbell, with careful espresso, good pastries and plenty of seats for working.

items.title: Nox Cookie Bar
items.why: Cookies served warm on Campbell's main street, until eleven at night: chocolate chip, lava cakes, lemon bars and cheesecake bites, with ice cream and affogato. Vegan and gluten-free cookies too.

items.title: Flower Flour
items.why: A bakery-café at the Pruneyard with breads, pastries, cakes and a full breakfast and lunch menu; one of the South Bay's best-known local bakeries.

items.title: Jiaren Café
items.why: A non-profit community café on Homestead Road: coffee, matcha, boba and fruit drinks, with cosy corners to sit and events in the evenings. Open until ten on weekdays.

items.title: Big Mug Coffee Roaster
items.why: A roaster on El Camino with warm wood, deep armchairs and plenty of room to read or work. Open until eleven most nights, which is rare around here.

items.title: Portuguese Tasty Desserts
items.why: A small family-run Portuguese bakery near El Camino and Main Street, from Santa Clara's long-standing Portuguese community. Go for the pastéis de nata, flaky custard tarts, and the sweet bread. Closes mid-afternoon.
items.source: portuguesetastydesserts.com; Silicon Valley Voice; Discover Santa Clara
items.coordsFrom: the address point for 1085 El Camino Real (osm way/416143550); the bakery is not mapped yet

items.title: Sue's Gallery Café
items.why: A café and pottery gallery at the top of Saratoga's village street: coffee and very good pastries served in handmade ceramics, with the pots for sale around you.

items.title: Big Basin Café
items.why: The village's everyday café on Big Basin Way: coffee, breakfast and sandwiches, and a patio on the street. Cyclists stop here on the way up Highway 9.

items.title: Saratoga Bagels
items.why: The town's bagel shop: bagels baked on site, spreads and breakfast sandwiches, busy on weekend mornings.

items.title: Alcatraz
items.why: The island prison in the middle of the bay, a federal penitentiary from 1934 to 1963 and now part of the Golden Gate National Recreation Area. The only way there is the Alcatraz City Cruises ferry from Pier 33, and tickets sell out weeks ahead, so book first. The cellhouse audio tour, narrated by former guards and prisoners, is included and is the reason to go. Leave time for the rest of the island too: the gardens the guards' families planted, the seabird colonies, and the graffiti from the Native American occupation of 1969 to 1971. The night tour is smaller and quieter, with the city lit up across the water.
items.priceNote: About $48 for the day tour and $60 for the night tour, ferry and audio tour included
items.source: nps.gov (Alcatraz Island); alcatrazcitycruises.com; confirmed against OpenStreetMap (relation/20197830)
items.hoursFrom: nps.gov: first ferry 8:45am; the island closes 6:30pm in summer and 4:30pm the rest of the year; shut on Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Year's Day

nightlife.note: Night places that do not expire — things only on after dark, live rooms, jazz, comedy and cabaret, dancing, bars, night markets and late-night food. Researched, not visited: every record says so. Programmes change nightly, so the link goes to the venue's own calendar; dated concerts belong in events.json.

items.title: SFJAZZ Center
items.why: The first free-standing building in America built for jazz, open since 2013. The main hall seats 350 to 700 depending on the set-up, and nowhere in it is far from the stage. The programme runs from legends to local players. Pick a night from the calendar.
items.hoursNote: Open for shows — the calendar is the timetable

items.title: Black Cat
items.why: A jazz supper club downstairs in the Tenderloin: live sets most nights, cocktails, and dinner at candlelit tables. San Francisco Magazine called it the city's most romantic spot. Book a table for the early set.
items.source: Black Cat; OpenTable; confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Punch Line
items.why: San Francisco's longest-running comedy club, open since 1978, and its only full-time one. Robin Williams, Ellen DeGeneres and Chris Rock worked out their acts here. The room is small enough that there are no bad seats.
items.source: Punch Line; Wikipedia; confirmed against OpenStreetMap
items.hoursNote: Open for shows — the calendar is the timetable

items.title: Cobb's Comedy Club
items.why: The bigger of the two stand-up rooms, in North Beach, where touring headliners play. Check the calendar, since who is on is the whole decision. Walk to Vesuvio afterwards.
items.hoursNote: Open for shows — the calendar is the timetable

items.title: BATS Improv
items.why: Improv at the Bayfront Theatre in Fort Mason on Saturday nights, with a short early show at 6:45 and the main one at 8. It is unscripted and different every time, and cheap enough to take a chance on. Coffee at Equator by the gate first.
items.source: Fort Mason Center; confirmed against OpenStreetMap
items.imageCredit: Original uploader was SuperJumbo at en.wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0
items.hoursNote: Main-stage shows on Saturday nights; improv.org has the season

items.title: The Fillmore
items.why: The ballroom where Bill Graham put on the Grateful Dead, Jefferson Airplane and Big Brother between 1965 and 1968. The walls are still covered with the posters. Go for whoever is playing, and arrive early to read the walls.
items.source: The Fillmore; FoundSF; confirmed against OpenStreetMap
items.hoursNote: Open for shows — the calendar is the timetable

items.title: Great American Music Hall
items.why: San Francisco's oldest nightclub, built in 1907 after the earthquake, with its gilded columns, carved balconies and original ceiling murals still in place. The room is as much the reason to go as the band.
items.hoursNote: Open for shows — the calendar is the timetable

items.title: Vesuvio
items.area: 255 Columbus Avenue, on Jack Kerouac Alley
items.why: The Beats' bar, opened in 1948 across the alley from City Lights. Kerouac, Ginsberg and Neal Cassady drank here, and Cassady stopped in on his way to the Six Gallery reading in 1955. It is a museum you can drink in. Buy a book at City Lights, then take it upstairs here.
items.source: Wikipedia; vesuvio.com; National Trust for Historic Preservation; confirmed against OpenStreetMap (way/35537202)

items.title: Tosca Cafe
items.why: Open since 1919, a red-leather room on Columbus. Order the house cappuccino, which isn't coffee at all but a Prohibition-era hot chocolate with bourbon and cognac. It was saved from closing and reopened with dinner. Go late and sit at the bar.
items.source: Tosca Cafe; SF Chronicle; confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Li Po Cocktail Lounge
items.why: Chinatown's oldest bar, open since 1937 and barely changed: red lanterns, a low ceiling and a Buddha shrine behind the bar. Order the Chinese mai tai. The recipe is a secret and uses a Chinese liqueur they make themselves.
items.hoursFrom: the Corner and SF Station listings

items.title: Smuggler's Cove
items.why: A three-storey tiki bar with more rums than any other bar in the country, over thirteen hundred. There are eighty cocktails on the menu, and it was named the best cocktail bar in the United States in 2016. Martin Cate, who founded it in 2009, wrote the book on rum. Go early, because it is small and the line forms.
items.source: Wikipedia; PUNCH; World's 50 Best; confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Trick Dog
items.why: The Mission cocktail bar that reinvents its whole menu around a theme every so often: a wrestling belt one year, a book of San Francisco photographs the next. It won the cocktail world's top award in 2025. Order off whatever the current menu is.
items.source: SF Standard; Axios; confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Zam Zam
items.why: A 1941 Persian Art Deco cocktail lounge in the Haight, opened as the Persian Aub Zam Zam, with arches and murals. For decades its owner famously ran it with an iron hand. Order a martini, which is what it is known for.
items.source: SF Heritage; SF Examiner; confirmed against OpenStreetMap
items.hoursFrom: the Yelp and Tripadvisor listings — Zam Zam has no website

items.title: The Rose & Crown
items.why: Palo Alto's oldest bar, an English pub on Emerson with more than twenty beers on tap, and fish and chips. Tuesday is trivia night: claim a table between 7:30 and 7:50, and the winners drink for free.
items.source: Palo Alto Online; confirmed against OpenStreetMap (way/133116331)

items.title: Dutch Goose
items.area: 3567 Alameda de las Pulgas, Menlo Park
items.why: The Stanford crowd's bar since 1966: peanut shells on the floor, burgers, pitchers, and deviled eggs made to the same recipe for sixty years. Order the eggs.
items.source: Stanford Magazine; M-A Chronicle; confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: British Bankers Club
items.why: A 1925 brick building by Birge Clark that has been a bank, Menlo Park's city hall and its jail. It has been a bar since 1977, now with a rooftop. Drink on the roof on a warm evening.
items.source: The Almanac; InMenlo; confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Frost Amphitheater
items.why: An outdoor bowl on the Stanford campus, from 1937, where 8,000 people sit on grass slopes above the stage. The summer and autumn concerts are the Peninsula's best big night out. Bring a blanket and a layer.
items.source: Stanford Live; Wikipedia; confirmed against OpenStreetMap
items.imageCredit: Bob Aronson from Monterey, CA, US · CC BY-SA 2.0
items.hoursNote: Open for shows — the calendar is the timetable

items.title: Bing Concert Hall
items.why: Stanford's concert hall, open since 2013: 842 seats in vineyard-style terraces around the stage, with acoustics by Yasuhisa Toyota. Stanford Live puts on classical, jazz and world music here. Every seat is close.
items.source: Stanford Live; Wikipedia; confirmed against OpenStreetMap
items.hoursNote: Open for shows — the calendar is the timetable

items.title: Exploratorium After Dark
items.hoursFrom: exploratorium.edu — After Dark, Thursdays 6 to 10pm, last entry 8:30
items.why: The science museum on Pier 15 with the children gone and a bar open. Every Thursday from six it is adults only, and the hundreds of hands-on exhibits are yours, down to the glass-walled observatory gallery over the bay. Each night has a theme and a talk or a DJ. It is the best first date in the city. Buy tickets ahead and arrive by eight, because last entry is 8:30.

items.title: NightLife at the Academy of Sciences
items.area: 55 Music Concourse Drive, Golden Gate Park
items.why: Thursday nights in Golden Gate Park: a four-storey rainforest under a glass dome, a coral reef, the penguins, and DJs and bars between them. It is 21 and over, so bring physical ID. Planetarium seats cost a few dollars more and go first, so reserve them with the ticket. Eat before you come or after; the park is dark and quiet by ten.

items.title: Audium
items.hoursFrom: audium.org — performances Thursday, Friday and Saturday at 8pm, doors 7:30
items.why: The only theatre of its kind in the world: forty-nine seats in a sloping room with 176 speakers in the walls, floor and ceiling, and the lights go out completely. Sound moves past you, over you and under you for about an hour. Stan Shaff began it in the late 1960s, and his son David now performs the pieces. Three nights a week at eight. Some tickets are sold in advance and a few pay-what-you-can seats go at the door from 7:30.

items.title: The Bay Lights
items.area: Best from Pier 14 or Pier 7, the Embarcadero
items.hoursFrom: illuminate.org — the lights run nightly from dusk to dawn
items.why: Forty-eight thousand LEDs on the cables of the Bay Bridge's western span, running patterns that never repeat. The piece went dark in 2023 and was relit on 20 March 2026, with a second strand added so it can be seen from more of the shore. Walk out to the end of Pier 14 or Pier 7 after sunset. It pairs with dinner at the Ferry Building, a ten-minute walk away.
items.imageSubject: The Bay Lights on the Bay Bridge

items.title: Telescope nights at Chabot
items.hoursFrom: chabotspace.org — free telescope viewings Friday and Saturday, 7:30 to 10:30pm
items.source: Chabot Space & Science Center; NASA Night Sky Network
items.why: Every Friday and Saturday night the observatory domes in the Oakland hills open for free, and you look through real telescopes: a refractor from 1883 named Leah, a 20-inch from 1916 named Rachel, and a 36-inch reflector. Volunteer astronomers point each one at something different and answer questions. If it is cloudy the domes are still open to tour; if it rains, stay home. Bring a layer: it is up in the redwoods.
items.firstStep: Free, no ticket — go round the back to the Observatory Deck

items.title: Castro Theatre
items.hoursNote: Open for shows and screenings — the calendar is the timetable
items.why: The 1922 movie palace under the neon sign, reopened on 6 February 2026 after a two-year, $41 million restoration. Another Planet now runs it for concerts, films, drag and comedy, with 1,400 seats that can be taken out for standing shows. The ceiling and the Wurlitzer organ are the reasons to go whatever is on. Frameline, the LGBTQ+ film festival, is here every June.

items.title: Bimbo's 365 Club
items.hoursNote: Open for shows — the calendar is the timetable
items.why: A 1931 supper club at the top of Columbus, still run by the family that opened it, and still one of the best-looking rooms a band can play in this city. The bookings run from indie bands to swing orchestras. It is a ten-minute walk up from Washington Square, and small enough that you will see the stage from anywhere.

items.title: The Independent
items.hoursNote: Open for shows — the calendar is the timetable
items.why: The room where bands play San Francisco on the way up: about five hundred standing, good sound, and nowhere far from the stage. Check the calendar a month out, because the names you will know next year sell it out. Divisadero is full of places to eat before a show, and the doors are usually at seven or eight.

items.title: Bottom of the Hill
items.hoursNote: Open for shows — the calendar is the timetable
items.why: A small rock club at the foot of Potrero Hill, open since 1991, where three bands a night play for a few hundred people and the ticket costs less than a cocktail downtown. A lot of bands that went on to fill arenas played here first. There is a patio out the back for between sets.

items.title: Shoreline Amphitheatre
items.priceNote: Lawn seats are the cheap way in
items.hoursNote: Open for shows, roughly April to October — the calendar is the timetable
items.why: The Peninsula's big outdoor stage: 22,000 people under a white tent roof and on a grass lawn by the bay in Mountain View. The season runs from spring into October, and this is where the arena tours stop. Buy a lawn ticket and bring a blanket. Leaving takes as long as the encore, so park facing the exit or cycle in on the Stevens Creek Trail.

items.title: Keys Jazz Bistro
items.hoursFrom: keysjazzbistro.com — Wednesday to Saturday, 5pm to 1am; sets at 7 and 9, and 11 on Saturday
items.why: Jazz back on Broadway, in a 125-seat room built around a Yamaha grand and a Hammond B3 organ. Sets are at seven and nine, with a late one at eleven on Saturday, and dinner is served at the tables. The booking leans to piano, organ trios and singers. It is all-ages, which almost no jazz room is, and two minutes from Vesuvio.

items.title: Dear San Francisco at Club Fugazi
items.hoursNote: Shows most evenings plus weekend matinées — check the calendar
items.why: A hundred minutes of circus about San Francisco, in the North Beach hall where Beach Blanket Babylon played for forty-five years. It is made by The 7 Fingers, whose founders grew up here: acrobats on poles and hoops a few feet from the front row, telling the city's story from the gold rush to now. Wine and small plates are sold inside. It is the best thing to take visitors to, and good without them.

items.title: Oasis
items.hoursNote: Open for shows and parties — the calendar is the timetable
items.why: San Francisco's drag cabaret, in a converted bathhouse on 11th Street, run by D'Arcy Drollinger since 2015. It nearly closed in 2025. A donation let it buy the building, and it reopened on 17 July 2026 with a new gold-tiled box office and pink curtains. There are staged shows early in the evening and dance parties after, and the full-length drag parodies of films and TV sell out first.

items.title: Rooster T. Feathers
items.hoursNote: Shows most nights — the calendar is the timetable
items.why: Silicon Valley's comedy club since 1984, on El Camino in Sunnyvale: a low-ceilinged room of small tables where touring headliners work out their hour. It is the one real stand-up room south of the city, so from Palo Alto it is fifteen minutes rather than an hour. Everyone is 21 and over, so bring ID, and buy tickets from the club's own site.

items.title: Public Works
items.hoursNote: Open for club nights, usually Thursday to Saturday from about 9:30pm — the calendar is the timetable
items.why: The city's serious dance floor: two rooms down an alley off Mission Street, a Funktion-One sound system, and house and techno DJs from Berlin, Detroit and the Bay on the same bill. It runs by the calendar rather than by the week, so check who is on. Nights start around half past nine and go late.

items.title: The EndUp
items.hoursNote: Open Thursday to Sunday; the Saturday party runs through Sunday morning — check the listings
items.why: The after-hours club, at the corner of 6th and Harrison since 1973. On Saturday night it keeps going through Sunday morning, and the point is walking out onto the garden patio into daylight. Everybody who stayed up too late in San Francisco for fifty years has ended up here. Go after one in the morning, never before.

items.title: El Rio
items.priceNote: Cheap · some nights have a cover
items.hoursNote: Open daily; Salsa Sunday on the second and fourth Sunday from 3pm
items.source: SF Legacy Business Registry; SF Station
items.why: A queer bar in the outer Mission since 1978, with one of the best back patios in the city: lemon trees, string lights and heaters, and room for a band and a crowd dancing. On the second and fourth Sunday of the month Salsa Sunday starts at three, with live salsa, merengue and cumbia bands. The rest of the week it is drag, karaoke, comedy and dance parties. The city has protected the patio as part of its Legacy Business listing.

items.title: Church of 8 Wheels
items.hoursFrom: churchof8wheels.com — adult sessions Friday and Saturday, 7 to 11pm
items.why: Roller disco in a deconsecrated church: a skating floor under the stained glass, a DJ and a disco ball. The Friday and Saturday evening sessions, seven to eleven, are for adults. Twenty dollars cash covers the skates. Nobody here is good at it, which is the point.

items.title: Tonga Room & Hurricane Bar
items.area: Fairmont Hotel, 950 Mason Street, Nob Hill
items.priceNote: Cocktails ~$20 · cover when the band plays
items.hoursFrom: fairmont-san-francisco.com — Wednesday and Thursday 5 to 10pm, Friday and Saturday 5 to 11pm
items.why: A tiki bar built in 1945 in the Fairmont's old swimming pool. The pool is now a lagoon, a band plays top-forty covers from a thatched barge on it from seven, and every half hour or so a tropical storm rolls through, with thunder, lightning and rain on the water. It is absurd and everyone should go once.

items.title: Top of the Mark
items.area: 19th floor, Mark Hopkins Hotel, Nob Hill
items.priceNote: Cocktails ~$20 · $15 cover for the Saturday band
items.hoursFrom: topofthemark.com — Sunday to Thursday 4 to 11pm, Friday and Saturday 3pm to 12:30am
items.why: The glass-walled bar on the nineteenth floor of the Mark Hopkins, open since 1939, where sailors shipping out in the Second World War had a last drink looking at the Golden Gate. The view goes all the way round: the bridge, the bay, the Financial District lit up. There is a band on Saturday nights. Come at sunset and take the window seats on the north side.

items.title: Specs'
items.hoursFrom: specsbarsf.com — daily from 4pm, to 2am Thursday to Saturday
items.source: Specs' Twelve Adler Museum Cafe; Wikipedia
items.why: A North Beach bar down a dead-end alley across Columbus from Vesuvio, open since 1968 and full of things sailors and regulars brought back: whale bones, walrus tusks, flags, and a case of oddities by the door. It is dim and argumentative, the way a bar used to be. Order a beer. Ask about anything on the walls.

items.title: Bourbon & Branch
items.hoursFrom: bourbonandbranch.com — 6pm to midnight Sunday to Wednesday, to 2am Thursday to Saturday
items.why: The speakeasy that started San Francisco's cocktail revival in 2006, behind an unmarked door on a Prohibition-era site. Book the main bar and you are sent a password for the night. The Library, at the back, takes walk-ins. The menu is long and the bartenders will make you something off it if you tell them what you like.

items.title: The Mint
items.priceNote: Drinks · a small tip per song
items.hoursFrom: The Mint — 5pm to 2am, from 4pm at weekends, closed Tuesday
items.why: The city's karaoke bar, singing since 1993. There are no private rooms: you sing to the whole bar from a proper stage, and the whole bar cheers. The book has 25,000 songs. Put your name down early, because by eleven on a Friday the wait is an hour. It is closed on Tuesdays.

items.title: The Patio
items.hoursNote: Opens at 11am every day and runs late at weekends — check the closing time before a late night
items.why: Downtown Palo Alto's outdoor bar: three open-air yards, the longest bar in town, and twenty-odd screens for whatever game is on. There is karaoke and trivia in the week. It is not a cocktail bar and does not pretend to be. It is where the Peninsula goes when it wants a loud night without driving to the city.

items.title: Chinatown Night Market
items.area: Grant Avenue and Waverly Place, Chinatown
items.priceNote: Free to walk; food from the stalls
items.hoursNote: Second Friday of the month, May to October, 5 to 9pm — the last of 2026 is 9 October
items.source: SF Funcheap; San Francisco Chinatown Merchants
items.why: Five blocks of Grant Avenue closed to cars on one Friday a month: street food, lion dancers, beer and wine gardens, and the shops staying open under the lanterns. It runs from five to nine, May to October, and 9 October is the last one this year. Start at the Dragon Gate on Bush and walk north, then finish with a mai tai at Li Po.

items.title: Fort Mason Night Market
items.area: Fort Mason Center, on the waterfront
items.hoursNote: One Friday a month, May to December, 5 to 10pm — next on 16 October, 6 November and 18 December
items.source: Fort Mason Center; Off the Grid; SF Funcheap
items.why: The old army piers on the Marina waterfront on a Friday night: a hundred-odd stalls of food trucks, makers and vintage, live music, and the Golden Gate going dark at the end of the quay. It is free and runs from five to ten on one Friday a month. The rest of 2026 is 16 October, 6 November and a holiday market on 18 December. Eat from the trucks, then have a drink at The Interval by the gate.
items.imageCredit: Original uploader was SuperJumbo at en.wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0

items.title: El Farolito
items.hoursFrom: elfarolitosf.com — daily to 2:45am, to 3:45am Friday and Saturday
items.why: The Mission burrito the city argues about, and the answer at two in the morning: open until 2:45 every night and 3:45 on Fridays and Saturdays. Order the super carne asada burrito, or the quesadilla suiza if you know. There are fluorescent lights and a queue out of the door after the bars shut, and it is right by the 24th Street BART.

items.title: Bob's Donuts
items.hoursFrom: bobsdonutssf.com — open 24 hours on Polk Street
items.why: A doughnut shop open twenty-four hours, where the fryers never stop and the apple fritter is the size of your face. It moved a few doors up Polk to 1720 but kept the hours, and at three in the morning it is the only warm, lit room on the street. There is a giant doughnut you can try to eat in under three minutes, if the night has gone that way.

items.title: Zareen's
items.hoursFrom: KQED; zareensrestaurant.com — daily 11am to midnight, takeout only after 11pm
items.why: Pakistani and Indian home cooking on California Avenue, and the rare Palo Alto kitchen still going at midnight, every night. It is the only one of Zareen's three restaurants that stays open late. Order the chicken tikka masala and the chapli kebab. It is takeout only after eleven, so eat in before then.

items.title: The Guild Theatre
items.hoursNote: Open for shows, doors usually 7pm and music at 8 — the calendar is the timetable
items.source: The Guild Theatre; The Almanac; Cinema Treasures
items.why: Menlo Park’s 1926 cinema, rebuilt inside its old walls and reopened in 2022 as a live-music room run by a non-profit. It holds about 500 standing or 200 seated, so touring bands that fill much bigger halls elsewhere play here at arm’s length. It is on El Camino, so from Palo Alto you are home ten minutes after the encore.

items.title: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
items.hoursNote: Open for performances — the calendar is the timetable
items.why: Three stages at the top of Castro Street: a 600-seat MainStage, a 200-seat SecondStage and the ParkStage. TheatreWorks Silicon Valley and Peninsula Youth Theatre are the resident companies, and dance, choirs, music and family shows fill the rest of the calendar. Dinner on Castro first and you walk to your seat.
items.imageSubject: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts

items.title: Open Mic Monday at Red Rock Coffee
items.area: Red Rock Coffee, 201 Castro Street, Mountain View (upstairs)
items.times: Every Monday, 6 to 9.30pm upstairs; lottery sign-ups 5.45 to 8pm. None on 28 December
items.firstStep: Put your name in the jar from 5.45pm for a five-minute set, or just come and listen
items.hoursNote: Every Monday, 6 to 9.30pm; sign-ups 5.45 to 8pm. None on 28 December
items.why: One of the Bay Area’s longest-running open mics, upstairs in a Castro Street coffee house every Monday night. Musicians, poets and comics draw five-minute slots by lottery, so nobody needs to queue early. It is kept family-friendly and has no age limit, so it works as a school-night outing with a teenager who plays. Go twice and you will start recognising the regulars.
items.imageSubject: Castro and Villa, the corner Red Rock Coffee stands on

items.title: Club Fox Blues Jam
items.times: Every Wednesday from 7pm: a featured band, then the jam
items.hoursNote: Every Wednesday from 7pm
items.why: A Wednesday-night blues jam that turned twenty in 2026, in the cabaret room beside Redwood City’s Fox Theatre. A regional or touring rhythm-and-blues band plays a set, then local players take the stage in turns. There are tables and a dance floor. It is the Peninsula’s steadiest weekly night of live music.
items.imageSubject: The Fox Theatre, next door on Broadway

items.title: Meyhouse Jazz
items.priceNote: Ticket for the show; dinner and drinks charged separately
items.cadence: Most Fridays and Saturdays, two seatings
items.times: Seatings at 5pm (show around 6:30) and 8pm (show around 8:30); each set runs about 75 minutes
items.hoursNote: Most Friday and Saturday nights; seatings at 5pm and 8pm
items.why: On most Friday and Saturday nights the Turkish restaurant on Emerson becomes a jazz supper club. The chef-owner books the music himself: touring trios and quartets, singers working through a songbook, and the odd classical Sunday. There are two seatings, at five and at eight, each with a set of about an hour and a quarter, and you eat meze while the band plays. Buy the ticket ahead; food and drink go on a separate bill. Along with the Club Fox jam, it is one of the few regular live rooms on the Peninsula.

items.title: Band Jam Night at The Hub
items.times: Every Tuesday, 8.30 to 10.30pm, on the upstairs stage
items.firstStep: Bring your instrument; the drums, keyboard and PA are there
items.hoursNote: Every Tuesday, 8.30 to 10.30pm
items.why: A standing Tuesday jam on a proper upstairs stage, with a full PA, drum kit and keyboard. You bring a guitar or a horn and join in with whoever turned up. There is no cover, and it is 21 and over. It is the place for the parent who used to be in a band.

items.title: Rossotti's Alpine Inn
items.why: A roadhouse in the foothills that has been pouring drinks since 1852, making it one of the oldest taverns in California and a state historical landmark. Stanford students have been driving up since the university opened; on a sunny weekend the big creekside beer garden fills with them, plus cyclists and families. Burgers, tacos and pitchers, ordered at the window.
items.source: alpineinnpv.com; Palo Alto Online (2024); Atlas Obscura; confirmed against OpenStreetMap
items.coordsFrom: the map pin for Rossotti's Alpine Inn

items.title: NOLA
items.why: A New Orleans restaurant and bar on Ramona, loud and colourful, with a big courtyard hung with lanterns. It's where Stanford groups go for birthdays and team dinners: jambalaya, gumbo, oysters and a long list of cocktails, with brunch at weekends.

items.title: Menlo Tavern
items.area: The Stanford Park Hotel, 100 El Camino Real, Menlo Park
items.why: The bar at the Stanford Park Hotel, on the Palo Alto line: leather, dark wood and a fire, with seasonal cocktails, local wines and upscale small plates. A polished, quiet place for a work drink that turns into dinner.

items.title: Bar Loretta
items.why: A small cocktail lounge on Santa Cruz Avenue, open since early 2025 and run with Bistro Vida next door. Classic and seasonal cocktails, wine by the glass, tapas and charcuterie; one of the few proper after-work bars in downtown Menlo Park.

items.title: canteenM at citizenM
items.why: The bar and canteen of the hotel Meta built on the edge of its campus at Willow Village, open since late 2023. It's open around the clock: coffee in the morning, cocktails and beer on tap in the evening, in a bright, bookish lobby full of laptops. The closest drink to Meta's offices.

items.title: Steins Beer Garden
items.why: A big beer garden just off Castro Street with dozens of taps, burgers and pretzels, and long tables under heaters. It's the default for a team drink in downtown Mountain View, and full of Googlers on a Thursday.
items.imageSubject: Castro Street at Villa, Mountain View

items.title: Ludwig's Biergarten
items.why: A proper German beer garden on Castro Street: litre steins of Bavarian beer, bratwurst, schnitzel and giant pretzels at communal tables outside. Loud and cheerful, and good for a big group.
items.source: ludwigsmv.com; Palo Alto Online (2021); confirmed against OpenStreetMap (way/205718455)
items.imageSubject: Castro Street at Villa, Mountain View

items.title: Rootstock Wine Bar
items.why: A relaxed wine bar on Castro with a long list by the glass, from California and beyond, and cheese and charcuterie boards to go with it. Quieter than the beer gardens around it: a good choice when you want to talk.
items.coordsFrom: the address point for 331 Castro Street (osm way/162342031); the bar is not mapped yet
items.imageSubject: Castro Street at Villa, Mountain View

items.title: Molly Magee's
items.why: The Irish pub on Castro and downtown Mountain View's late-night bar: Guinness, pool, darts and a small dance floor, open until two every night.
items.imageSubject: Castro Street at Villa, Mountain View

items.title: Madera at Rosewood Sand Hill
items.why: The restaurant and bar of the hotel at the top of Sand Hill Road, where the venture capital firms are, which makes it the investors' quiet alternative to Buck's. Wood-fired Californian cooking, a wine list of well over a thousand bottles and a terrace looking west to the Santa Cruz Mountains. It held a Michelin star until 2022.
items.source: rosewoodhotels.com; SFGate; the Michelin Guide; confirmed against OpenStreetMap (way/384022279)

items.title: The Duke of Edinburgh
items.why: A proper English pub a few minutes from Apple Park, and the Apple crowd's pint after work for decades: dark wood, darts, British beers on tap, and fish and chips in several sizes.

sports.note: Hand-written. Play is what you can do — lessons, pools, courts, gyms and group runs; Trails are hikes and rides; Watch is where the teams play, with dated fixtures in events.json. Researched, not visited.

items.title: The Dish loop
items.area: Stanford Avenue trailhead · 3.7 mi loop · about 530 ft up
items.why: A 3.7-mile paved loop over the Stanford foothills past a 150-foot radio telescope, with views across the whole Bay. It climbs more than it looks (about 530 feet). There is almost no shade and very little parking, so go early and bring water. The gates open and close with the daylight, and the times change by month.
items.source: AllTrails; Destination Palo Alto; Wikipedia; trailhead confirmed against OpenStreetMap (node/4562251453)
items.hoursFrom: destinationpaloalto.com — the Dish is open sunrise to sunset
items.hoursNote: Sunrise to sunset
items.dogsNote: No dogs on the Dish trail, service animals excepted (Stanford)

items.title: Pearson-Arastradero Preserve
items.area: Arastradero Road lot · 3.7 mi loop · about 300 ft up · bikes allowed on its wide trails
items.why: The gentlest hike in Palo Alto: open grassland and oak hills a few minutes past 280, with ten miles of trail to choose from. The Arastradero Creek loop goes out along the Juan Bautista de Anza trail and back by Acorn and Meadowlark. It is good for birds, and the loop to do when you want to be walking in twenty minutes. Some trails close after rain.
items.source: POST (Peninsula Open Space Trust); AllTrails; preserve confirmed against OpenStreetMap (relation/10781180)
items.hoursFrom: paloalto.gov — the city's open spaces are open 8am to sunset
items.hoursNote: 8am to sunset
items.dogsNote: On a leash, under physical control (City of Palo Alto)

items.title: Foothills Nature Preserve
items.area: Page Mill Road entrance · 15 miles of trail
items.priceNote: Entry rules and a daily cap — check before you go
items.why: Palo Alto's own mountain park: fifteen miles of trail in the foothills, with Boronda Lake and Vista Hill. From the top of Vista Hill, on a clear day, you can see Hoover Tower, the Dumbarton Bridge, Mount Diablo and Mount Hamilton. It was for Palo Alto residents only for fifty-one years and opened to everyone in December 2020. Visitor numbers are still capped, so check the city's page for the current rules.
items.source: City of Palo Alto; San Francisco Chronicle; Palo Alto Online; confirmed against OpenStreetMap (relation/6258591)
items.hoursFrom: paloalto.gov — the city's open spaces are open 8am to sunset
items.hoursNote: 8am to sunset
items.dogsNote: Dogs on weekdays only — not on weekends or city holidays (City of Palo Alto, Municipal Code 22.04.150)

items.title: Windy Hill — Spring Ridge Trail
items.area: Portola Road lot · 5.6 mi · about 1,370 ft up
items.why: The climb the Peninsula knows by sight: the bare green hill above Portola Valley. Go up Spring Ridge Trail from the Portola Road lot to the top, where the whole bay spreads out below. It is steep and open, so go early. For a longer day, make it a 7.5-mile loop down Hamms Gulch through the woods.
items.source: Midpeninsula Regional Open Space District; POST; AllTrails; preserve confirmed against OpenStreetMap (relation/193017)
items.hoursFrom: openspace.org — half an hour before sunrise until half an hour after sunset
items.hoursNote: Half an hour before sunrise to half an hour after sunset
items.dogsNote: Leash of 6 ft or less, and only on Spring Ridge, Betsy Crowder, Sequoias, Eagle, Meadow, Hamms Gulch and Anniversary trails (Midpen)

items.title: Rancho San Antonio — PG&E Trail
items.area: Cristo Rey Drive lots · 4.3 mi loop · about 700 ft up
items.why: The busiest trailhead on the Peninsula, for good reason. There are loops of every length, from an easy walk to Deer Hollow Farm (baby goats in spring) up to eleven-plus miles up the PG&E Trail. The classic is the PG&E, Wildcat and Coyote loop. The one catch is parking: on a summer weekend the lots are full by eight, so arrive before that.
items.source: Midpeninsula Regional Open Space District; Hilltromper; AllTrails; preserve confirmed against OpenStreetMap (way/296113630)
items.imageSubject: Rancho San Antonio Open Space Preserve
items.hoursFrom: openspace.org — half an hour before sunrise until half an hour after sunset
items.hoursNote: Half an hour before sunrise to half an hour after sunset

items.title: Purisima Creek Redwoods
items.area: Skyline Boulevard or Purisima Creek Road · 4.8 to 10.5 mi loops
items.why: The nearest proper redwood forest to Palo Alto, on the ocean side of Skyline. The 4.8-mile Grabtown Gulch and Borden Hatch Mill loop goes through second-growth redwoods. The full day is about ten miles down the creek and back up. There is also a quarter-mile flat, wheelchair-accessible path through tall redwoods right off Skyline. It is often in fog, so bring a layer.
items.source: Midpeninsula Regional Open Space District; Bay Area Ridge Trail; confirmed against OpenStreetMap (relation/193021)
items.imageSubject: Purisima Creek Redwoods Open Space Preserve
items.hoursFrom: openspace.org — half an hour before sunrise until half an hour after sunset
items.hoursNote: Half an hour before sunrise to half an hour after sunset

items.title: Mori Point
items.why: A short coastal loop over a headland in Pacifica, with the Pacific on three sides. You climb the steep Bootlegger's Steps to the top of the bluff, named for the Prohibition smugglers who landed here. It takes an hour, so it works as a morning before breakfast, or as the walk to end a day on the coast.
items.source: Golden Gate National Parks Conservancy; AllTrails; confirmed against OpenStreetMap (relation/3923236)
items.hoursFrom: nps.gov — the trails are open around the clock, the car parks sunrise to sunset
items.hoursNote: The trails never close; the car park is open sunrise to sunset

items.title: Tennessee Valley to the beach
items.area: Mill Valley, end of Tennessee Valley Road · 3.4 mi out and back
items.why: An easy, nearly flat walk down a green valley to a small cove beach on the Pacific, 1.7 miles each way. The first half-mile is paved. It is the Marin hike for a slow morning or for anyone who doesn't want to climb. The lot fills fast at weekends, and cars end up parked far down the road.
items.source: AllTrails; Marin County Visitor; road confirmed against OpenStreetMap (way/659312700)
items.coordsFrom: osm way/659312700 (end of Tennessee Valley Road)
items.hoursFrom: nps.gov — the trails are open around the clock, the car parks sunrise to sunset
items.hoursNote: The trails never close; the car park is open sunrise to sunset

items.title: Steep Ravine & Matt Davis loop
items.area: Stinson Beach trailhead · about 6.4 mi · about 1,900 ft up
items.why: The best loop on Mount Tamalpais, and a full morning. Go up the Matt Davis Trail from Stinson Beach, through forest and then out onto grassland high above the Pacific. Come down Steep Ravine, past waterfalls and redwoods and down the famous wooden ladder. It climbs about 1,900 feet. Finish in the sea at Stinson.
items.source: Golden Gate National Parks Conservancy; Bay Area Hiker; AllTrails; trail confirmed against OpenStreetMap (way/1442270016)
items.hoursFrom: parks.ca.gov — Mount Tamalpais State Park, 7am to sunset
items.hoursNote: 7am to sunset

items.title: Over the Golden Gate to Sausalito
items.area: From Aquatic Park · about 8 mi · paths, some road, hills at the bridge
items.priceNote: Bike hire from the Wharf; ferry back ~$15
items.why: The classic ride. From Aquatic Park it runs along the water through Fort Mason, the Marina and Crissy Field, climbs to the bridge and crosses it, then drops down into Sausalito. Take the ferry back instead of climbing home. In 2026 that means the Golden Gate Ferry to the Ferry Building, because the Blue & Gold boat to Pier 41 isn't running while its dock is repaired. Bike hire is all along Fisherman's Wharf.
items.source: Blazing Saddles; OurSausalito; Inside Guide to San Francisco Tourism; start confirmed against OpenStreetMap (way/32839638)
items.hoursNote: Bikes may cross the bridge at any hour, through gates at night; the ferry back runs to a timetable

items.title: Golden Gate Park to Ocean Beach
items.area: JFK Promenade from the Conservatory · 3.4 mi each way · car-free, paved
items.priceNote: Free; bike share at the park
items.why: The easy one, and entirely in the city. JFK Drive through Golden Gate Park has been car-free since 2020, made permanent in 2022. Start at the Conservatory of Flowers and roll west past the museums and lakes all the way to the ocean. It is a gentle downhill out and a gentle climb back. Carry on along the Great Highway path by Ocean Beach if you have the legs.
items.source: SF Recreation & Parks; TrailLink; start confirmed against OpenStreetMap (way/30675038)
items.hoursFrom: San Francisco Park Code §3.21 — city parks close from midnight to 5am
items.routeEndFrom: the Beach Chalet at Ocean Beach, osm node/417235672 (Nominatim)

items.title: Sawyer Camp Trail
items.area: Crystal Springs Dam · 6 mi each way · paved, car-free
items.why: Six miles of paved, car-free trail along Crystal Springs Reservoir, in the rift valley of the San Andreas Fault. It is halfway between San Francisco and Palo Alto, so it works from either. Halfway along is the Jepson Laurel, more than six hundred years old and the oldest in California. It is shared with walkers and runners, so ride it slow. The county has closed it for storm and culvert repairs before, so check its advisories first.
items.source: County of San Mateo; Wikipedia; trail confirmed against OpenStreetMap (way/791183517)
items.hoursFrom: San Mateo County Parks, via Bay Area Hiker
items.hoursNote: Sunrise to sunset
items.routeEndFrom: Hillcrest Boulevard, Millbrae, the north trailhead, osm way/464920592 (Nominatim)

items.title: The Bay Trail: Baylands to Shoreline
items.area: Palo Alto Baylands · flat · gravel and crushed shell, some paved
items.why: Flat riding along the edge of the bay from the Palo Alto Baylands south to Shoreline Park in Mountain View, past salt ponds and marsh, with birds the whole way. The surface is mostly gravel and crushed shell with some paved stretches, so a hybrid is better than a road bike. Shoreline has ten more miles of paths around its lake. The Stevens Creek Trail, paved and off-street, runs inland from there if you want more.
items.source: Bay Trail (MTC); City of Mountain View; MTB Project; start confirmed against OpenStreetMap
items.coordsFrom: the Baylands interpretive center (on the site already)
items.hoursFrom: paloalto.gov — the city's open spaces are open 8am to sunset; Shoreline in Mountain View keeps its own
items.hoursNote: 8am to sunset

items.title: The Stevens Creek Trail
items.area: Crittenden Lane to Yuba Drive, Mountain View · flat · paved, off-street
items.why: A paved path along Stevens Creek from Shoreline Park south through Mountain View, passing under 101, Middlefield and Highway 85 and over Central Expressway, so you never wait at a junction with cars. It joins the Bay Trail at the top, which makes it the car-free way between downtown Mountain View, Shoreline and the Baylands. The speed limit is 15 mph and bikes give way to people on foot, so it suits a child on their own bike.
items.source: City of Mountain View; Friends of Stevens Creek Trail
items.coordsFrom: Crittenden Lane, where it meets Shoreline, osm way/685522097 (Nominatim)
items.routeEndFrom: the Yuba Drive trailhead, osm way/8957394 (Nominatim)
items.hoursFrom: mountainview.gov — trails open 6am to half an hour after sunset
items.hoursNote: 6am to half an hour after sunset; underpasses can close for flooding in winter

items.title: The Portola Loop
items.area: Sand Hill, Portola and Alpine roads · about 11.5 mi · on the road
items.why: The loop every Peninsula road cyclist knows: Sand Hill, Portola and Alpine roads round Portola Valley, about eleven and a half miles, and packed with riders on weekend mornings. The locals argue about which direction to ride it. It is on the road with cars, with bike lanes most of the way. Ride it early at weekends, when it is mostly other cyclists.
items.source: Palo Alto Bicycles; Bo Crane Books; Strava; confirmed against OpenStreetMap (way/40187960)

items.title: Old La Honda climb
items.area: Portola Road, by the stone bridge · 3 mi · just under 8%
items.why: The Peninsula's benchmark climb, for when the loop isn't enough. It is almost exactly three miles at just under eight percent, from the stone bridge off Portola Road up to Skyline, through redwoods and tanoak. The road is narrow and there is some traffic. Come down the way you went up, carefully, or carry on over Skyline for a long day.
items.source: Palo Alto Bicycles; Komoot; road confirmed against OpenStreetMap (way/941162598)

items.title: Giants at Oracle Park
items.priceNote: Cheap seats in the bleachers; more behind home plate
items.times: MLB, April to late September, most days in season
items.transit: Muni Metro to 2nd & King, or Caltrain to 4th & King
items.why: The best-placed ballpark in America, on the bay at the edge of SoMa. A home run to right field lands in the water of McCovey Cove, where kayakers wait for it. Get bleacher seats and watch the sun go down over the city behind the outfield. Bring a jacket to a night game: it is cold by the fourth inning.
items.source: San Francisco Giants; Wikipedia; confirmed against OpenStreetMap
items.hoursNote: Game days only — the schedule is the timetable

items.title: Warriors and Valkyries at Chase Center
items.priceNote: Warriors are expensive; Valkyries much less so
items.times: Warriors, October to April; Valkyries (WNBA), May to September
items.transit: Muni T Third to the UCSF/Chase Center stop
items.why: The arena in Mission Bay, open since 2019, and home to two teams. The Warriors are the famous ticket. The Valkyries are the better night out: the WNBA's newest team, a sold-out crowd from their first season, and in 2026 one of the best records the league has seen. The waterfront park outside is good before the game.
items.source: Chase Center; SF Standard; confirmed against OpenStreetMap
items.hoursNote: Game days only — the schedule is the timetable

items.title: 49ers at Levi's Stadium
items.priceNote: NFL prices; the upper deck is the way in
items.times: NFL, September to January, home games roughly every other Sunday
items.transit: Caltrain to Mountain View, then VTA light rail to Great America
items.why: The 49ers' stadium in Santa Clara, open since 2014, which hosted the Super Bowl in 2016 and again in February 2026. Tailgating in the lots is half the day. Take the train rather than driving: the car parks empty very slowly.
items.source: Levi's Stadium; San Francisco 49ers; confirmed against OpenStreetMap
items.hoursNote: Game days only — the schedule is the timetable

items.title: Stanford football at Stanford Stadium
items.priceNote: Among the cheapest big-stadium tickets in the Bay
items.times: College football, September to November, home Saturdays
items.transit: Caltrain to Palo Alto and walk across campus, or the free Marguerite shuttle
items.why: Big-time college football you can walk to from downtown Palo Alto. The stadium sits in a grove of trees on campus, with the band and a crowd of students. Tickets are easy to get and cheap by the standard of the pros. Make a day of it: lunch on University Avenue, the game, and the Rodin garden on the way home.
items.hoursNote: Game days only — the schedule is the timetable

items.title: Lawn bowling in Golden Gate Park
